Deal value

slides.sub: Cushman & Wakefield Q3 2026 Marketbeat, via Gulf Times

captions.linkedin:
Qatar's residential deals barely slowed in Q3. Their value fell 28%.

According to Cushman & Wakefield's Q3 2026 Marketbeat for Qatar, reported by Gulf Times, residential transaction volumes dropped by just 2.5% in the third quarter. The aggregate value of residential transactions fell 28.0%, to about QR3.18bn.

Volumes almost flat, value sharply down. That points to smaller tickets on average.

Why it matters for agencies:
If the average deal is worth less, each commission is smaller. To keep revenue steady, the same team has to close more deals, or lose fewer of the leads it already has.

What to do now:
• Cut the time between a new enquiry and the first reply
• Keep every listing live and accurate on each portal you use
• Know your conversion rate by agent and by lead source
• Remove admin that keeps agents away from viewings

Efficiency matters more when value per deal shrinks. (It's the problem we built OneLinker CRM to solve.)

Is your team chasing more deals this quarter, or bigger ones?
